title: Fallout Janus Bear / Garden Gnome Proxy-Actor and Miniature-Diorama Grammar

fallout3.general_finding: Fallout 3 gnomes occur in multiple sizes and are deliberately positioned interacting with teddy bears or playing roles.

teddy + miniature intact gnome watch miniature TV with cigarettes, shot glass and vodka

cross_game_nodes.finding: One evil-gnome variant is a direct behind-the-scenes reference to lead world builder Scott Everts.
cross_game_nodes.boundary: This does not make every gnome a developer avatar.

cross_game_nodes.node: seven intact gnomes around red crystals
cross_game_nodes.finding: Seven gnomes are staged as miners around red crystals with pickaxes and lanterns.
cross_game_nodes.boundary: No causal or lore identity is established between these red crystals and Mothership Zeta alien crystals.

cross_game_nodes.finding: Gnomes are repeatedly positioned in amusing or horrifying tableaux, including open-grave/skeleton/camera/fishing arrangements.
Gnomes are staged in audience/mischief/death scenes; a broken gnome stands over a skeleton with a knife in its chest.
An unmarked garden contains three garden gnomes and a Quantum bear.

combined_grammar: GNOME + CRYSTAL + TOOLS -> MINIATURE LABOR/RESOURCE ROLE

janus_bear_connection.structural_inversion: Fallout often leaves the teddy as a powerless witness after catastrophe; Janus Bear is intentionally specified as a nonviolent companion intended to summon human protection before catastrophe.
janus_bear_connection.gnome_design_lesson: The gnome demonstrates how a tiny inanimate object can carry actor/observer semantics through pose alone; Janus Bear must not confuse symbolic agency with real authority.
